title: Azure Functions Overview
description: Introduction to serverless functions in ASP.NET Core — what they are, when to use them, and the .NET programming model.

data.text: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service that runs your code on demand without provisioning or managing infrastructure. You write a C# method, Azure handles the rest — scaling, patching, and billing by execution.
Serverless doesn't mean "no servers" — it means you don't manage them. Azure provisions compute only while your function runs. When idle, you pay nothing.

data.title: Key characteristics
items: **Event-driven** — functions run in response to HTTP requests, timers, queue messages, or blobs
**Auto-scaling** — Azure adds or removes instances based on incoming load
**Pay-per-execution** — you are billed only for the time your code runs
**Stateless by default** — each invocation is independent; state lives in external services

data.text: A **trigger** starts a function — for example, an HTTP request or a timer. A **binding** is a declarative way to connect your function to another Azure service without writing connection code.

data.title: In-process vs isolated process
data.text: This course uses the **isolated worker model** — your Functions run in a separate process from the Azure Functions runtime. This gives you full control over dependencies, DI, and target framework. The older in-process model is still supported but is not recommended for new projects.

cards.title: In-process
cards.description: Functions run inside the same process as the Azure Functions runtime.

cards.title: Isolated worker (recommended)
cards.description: Functions run in a separate process, communicating with the runtime over gRPC.

data.title: Good fits
items: HTTP APIs with bursty or unpredictable traffic
File processing after upload to Blob Storage
Scheduled data cleanup or report generation
Reactive workflows responding to queue or event messages

data.title: Avoid when
items: You need long-running stateful processes (use Durable Functions instead)
Cold-start latency is unacceptable (use App Service or AKS)
You need full control over the runtime environment

data.title: Package references for Azure Functions
data.content: Add these NuGet packages to your Functions project.
data.code:
dotnet new worker --name MyFunctionApp --output ./MyFunctionApp
cd MyFunctionApp

# Core worker SDK
# Package: Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker
# Package: Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker.Extensions.Http
# Package: Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Functions is event-driven serverless compute for C#
The isolated worker model is recommended for new projects
Triggers start a function; bindings connect it to other services declaratively
Functions scale automatically and you only pay for execution time
data.takeaway: Azure Functions is the natural complement to ASP.NET Core when you need event-driven or scheduled workloads without managing servers.
